title: Treasure in Jars of Clay - Part Two
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro

outline.title: The Eternal Weight of Glory
subpoints: Distinguishing the perishing outward man from the renewing inward man
Viewing temporary affliction as producing eternal glory
The hope of a heavenly building from God, not made with hands

outline.title: Living in Light of the Resurrection
subpoints: Confidence in being absent from the body and present with the Lord
The intermediate state as a transition, not the final destination
The aim to be well-pleasing to God whether present or absent

outline.title: The Compelling Love of Christ
subpoints: The fear of God and the love of Christ as motivating forces
The exchange: Christ made sin for us that we might become righteousness
The theological hinge of the gospel: substitutionary atonement

outline.title: The Ministry of Reconciliation
subpoints: God reconciling the world to Himself in Christ
Believers as ambassadors carrying the message of reconciliation
The urgency of the 'now' as the day of salvation

outline.title: The Paradoxes of Ministry
subpoints: Enduring hardships: distress, imprisonment, and labor
Sustained by spiritual resources: purity, kindness, and the Holy Spirit
The paradox of being poor yet making many rich

outline.title: The Appeal for Open Hearts
subpoints: Identifying narrowness and restriction in the Corinthian believers
The need for an enlarged heart to receive the gospel
The danger of resentment and isolation in a closed heart

summary: In this second installment of the 'Treasure in Jars of Clay' series, Pastor Tito Lyro continues tracing the thread of 2 Corinthians, focusing on the final movements of the first half of the letter. The sermon addresses the question of what happens when the 'jar' of the human body finally breaks, emphasizing that while the outward man perishes, the inward man is renewed day by day. Paul’s confidence stems from the assurance that light, temporary afflictions are working out an eternal weight of glory, shifting the believer’s focus from the seen and temporary to the unseen and eternal.
